summary:
Ember Atlas is an integrated wildfire intelligence platform and harmonized database that bridges 25+ years of NASA satellite observations. Currently, wildfire data comes from two incompatible sensor generations: MODIS and VIIRS, that capture fires at different resolutions, making direct historical comparisons impossible. With MODIS retiring in 2027, over a decade of vital fire history risks becoming disconnected from modern records. To solve this, we developed a machine learning harmonization model, achieving a 4–6% monthly error rate compared to 14–23% for standard ratio methods, that unifies records from four satellites onto a single scale with a unified confidence metric, even accounting for Aqua’s orbital drift.
For farmers and landowners, Ember Atlas turns raw satellite data into actionable protection: users can drop a pin on any plot to generate historical fire frequency, seasonality, and risk reports before buying land, followed by near-real-time fire alerts and emergency reporting. For researchers, it provides an open-access (CSV/JSON) harmonized dataset to objectively track climate-driven fire trends and validate predictive models without sensor bias.
details:
Ember Atlas is a unified wildfire intelligence platform that bridges 25+ years of Earth observation data from two fundamentally different generations of NASA satellites: MODIS and VIIRS into a single, reliable decision-making and research tool.

  • How It Works: We recognized that MODIS and VIIRS capture fundamentally different types of information and operate at different spatial resolutions, meaning their raw records cannot be directly compared. To solve this, we harmonized the datasets by training a machine learning model to learn the non-linear ratio and relationship between both sensors (achieving a 4–6% monthly error rate compared to 14–23% with simple ratio scaling). Using this model, we converted pre-2012 MODIS records into a VIIRS-equivalent scale and merged them with 2012–2025 observations. We also built a unified confidence system using pairs of primary satellites spaced 90 minutes apart—when one satellite detects a fire, the trailing satellite cross-verifies its accuracy—while explicitly separating true zero-fire days from "no-data" days so orbital gaps aren't mistaken for safety. Finally, we built an interactive web calendar and map where users can filter trends across any month and year, drop a pin on any plot of land to generate custom fire frequency and risk reports, and receive near-real-time fire alerts.
  • Benefits & Intended Impact: With MODIS retiring in 2027, over a decade of critical historical fire data risks becoming disconnected from modern records. For farmers and landowners, Ember Atlas provides an essential due-diligence tool to evaluate wildfire risk before investing in land: helping prevent devastating losses like Australia's 2019–20 Black Summer: alongside continuous post-purchase monitoring and emergency reporting. For scientists, it delivers an open-access (CSV/JSON) harmonized database to objectively study climate-driven fire trends and validate predictive models without sensor bias.
  • Creativity & Key Considerations: Rather than treating satellite passes as isolated snapshots, we creatively leveraged the natural 90-minute orbital offset between satellite pairs as an automated physical fact-checker. We also accounted for real-world orbital mechanics, such as NASA's Aqua satellite drifting in orbit by over an hour and validated our model across unseen decade-apart years to ensure long-term stability.
